correctness.finding: The counterexample is correct. For s≥20, t=s² and N=s⁶, the primitive normal set has enough directions, D=3s(t−1)+1≤3s³, all indexed planes remain distinct modulo any prime p≥s⁴, and each grid point contributes exactly once for every normal. Selecting the N richest planes gives I≥N²/D≥N^{3/2}/3, hence I/N^{17/12}≥N^{1/12}/3→∞. The modular distinctness and no-wrap conditions are valid.

originality.finding: Known point–plane incidence theorems give the O(N^{3/2}) scale for general configurations, and Euclidean lattice-grid work constructs other point–hyperplane incidence lower bounds, but the search found no prior result that supplies this equal-size prime-field Cartesian-cube family with the small-primitive-normal averaging argument and Ω(N^{3/2}) incidences in the regime N≤p^{3/2}. The closest lattice-incidence paper has different hypotheses/objective and, in d=3 with equal m,n, a weaker K_{r,r}-free exponent.

scientific_value.finding: The construction directly resolves the admitted two-sided target by disproving any uniform N^{17/12} bound with an absolute constant, and it does so on the restrictive Cartesian-grid point set. The argument is short but structural and reusable: it identifies a concrete small-normal plane family saturating the N^{3/2} scale.
